title: Code Reviewer dispatch webhook, version 1
description: The signed wake-up call of the Webhook-Trigger (#316, #318): after a job is enqueued the app sends POST <dispatch URL> to the Dispatcher, which then claims exactly that job (claim by job id is the idempotency point; a replay finds a job that is not due and gets 204). The body is DispatchWebhook: closed, at most 1 KiB, no secret and no repository data. Headers: Content-Type: application/json; X-Dispatch-Timestamp (Unix seconds, decimal); X-Dispatch-Id (the dispatchId of the body); X-Dispatch-Key-Id (which signing key, to rotate with a current and a previous key); X-Dispatch-Signature: 'v1=' followed by the lower case hexadecimal HMAC-SHA-256, keyed with the secret of that key id (UTF-8 text), over the UTF-8 text 'v1:{timestamp}:{dispatchId}:{rawBody}' where rawBody is the request body exactly as sent. The signing secret is distinct from every other secret. A receiver checks, in this order: content type and size; the headers' form (malformed); the timestamp within the tolerance of its own clock, 300 seconds either way (expired); the key id against its current and previous key (unknown_key); the signature in constant time (bad_signature); only then parses the body against DispatchWebhook (closed schema) and requires its dispatchId to equal the header. The verdicts and a vector for each are in dispatch-signing-vectors.json (DispatchSigningVectors). A receiver answers at once: 202 DispatchAccepted, 200 DispatchIgnored, 429 or 503 with Retry-After, and 401/400/413 with the runner API's ErrorResponse for what it refuses, the same for every kind of refusal. Both ends read this file: the app (app/integration-tests/compatibility), the runner (runner/tests/contract) and the Dispatcher project check its examples.

DispatchWebhook.description: The body of the wake-up call. Closed: an unknown field, such as a secret, a token, a credential, a signature or repository data, is refused. A sender never adds one and a receiver refuses a body that has one.

attempt.description: The number of the attempt the job is on (1 for the first).

dispatchId.description: The id of this call, new for every send of the same job (a UUID).

KnownDispatchIgnoredReason.description: Why a receiver answered 200 ignored. `not_claimable`: the claim of that job answered 204 (not due, running, finished, cancelled, superseded, or the pool cap is reached); the app resends after its acknowledgement timeout. `not_capable`: the receiver cannot run that review kind; the app stops resending that kind. A reader accepts any reason of the right form.

DispatchAccepted.description: 202 from the receiver: the wake-up call is verified and the claim goes on in the background.

DispatchIgnored.description: 200 from the receiver: verified, and there is nothing to start.

DispatchSigningVectors.description: The file dispatch-signing-vectors.json: signing keys of the example (dummy values), the tolerance, and requests as a receiver sees them with the verdict each must get. A consumer (the app's sender and the Dispatcher's receiver, in TypeScript, and the runner suite in Python) computes the verdict itself and compares. Header names are lower case.

body.description: The raw body exactly as received.

DispatchSigningKey.description: A signing key of the example. The secret is a dummy; a real one is at least 32 characters and unique to this purpose.
